title: Building Connected vs. Downtobid - A Side-By-Side Comparison
summary: Explore a detailed comparison of Building Connected and Downtobid, highlighting key features, usability, and how they streamline construction bidding
body_text: Building Connected and Downtobid are two notable invitation to bid softwares in the construction industry. From creating bid invites and finding qualified subcontractors, these platforms are what general contractors need. But how do they compare against each other? This Building Connected vs. Downtobid guide will go over the different features of each platform separately and what makes them unique. Note: Speed up your bid invitations with Downtobid. This software automates personalized bid invitations to the right contractors, proposes sending times and allows subs to access plans without creating an account. The tool can increase subcontractor participation by up to 30%. Start your free trial now. Key Takeaways Downtobid gets 30% higher response rates with personalized invites; BuildingConnected uses mass blasts. Downtobid maintains verified data; BuildingConnected has outdated self-managed profiles. Downtobid offers organized, no-login planrooms; BuildingConnected has cluttered interfaces requiring accounts. BuildingConnected provides enterprise integrations but costs more with added complexity. Reddit users prefer Downtobid's reliability over BuildingConnected's outdated contacts and pricing. From Collaboration to Chaos: How Bidding Got Messy There was a time when construction bidding was all about relationships. GCs and trade contractors would meet face-to-face, share plans, and collaborate on projects in a straightforward, respectful way. But as technology took over, the process became less personal and more chaotic. Platforms promised efficiency but instead delivered a flood of irrelevant invites, spammy ITBs, and mismanaged workflows. Contractors now ignore most bid invites, overwhelmed by the sheer volume, while GCs lose valuable time chasing responses and managing outdated contact lists. This frustration has led many in the industry to rethink how bidding should work. Platforms like Downtobid and BuildingConnected each offer a way forward—but they take very different approaches to solving the problem. What is Downtobid? Downtobid is an AI-powered ITB tool and bid management software built to eliminate guesswork in the bidding process. Rather than blasting invites to random contractors and hoping they’ll respond, Downtobid focuses on forging reliable partners by matching each job to the right subcontractors. Its features include: Personalized ITBs that highlight relevant scopes, so trades see only what they need. Automated follow-ups that nudge subs if they haven’t replied, reducing last-minute scrambles. A curated subcontractor network with valid contact data, preventing GCs from hunting down outdated leads. Light plan “sheeting” that helps subcontractors quickly identify the relevant sections, cutting labor requirements for reviewing documents. Because it keeps invites accurate and fosters a direct connection with subs, Downtobid preserves the human side of bidding. GCs avoid spamming dozens of random addresses and can proceed more confidently, trusting that the subs who do respond are genuinely interested. What is BuildingConnected? BuildingConnected has been a staple in the construction industry for years, offering a broad, all-in-one platform for managing bids. Its massive network of trade contractors, prequalification tools, and integrations with platforms like Autodesk make it a popular choice for large-scale projects. BuildingConnected is often used by builders seeking a broader subcontractor network. It’s known for: A massive database of contractors in diverse locations, ideal if you frequently expand or handle multi-state projects. Deep integrations with Autodesk and other collaboration tools, letting bigger teams unify data, scheduling, and cost analysis in one system. Prequalification modules that can help with risk oversight, plus optional takeoff tools for early estimates. The best features of BuildingConnected appear when you run huge coverage blasts or rely on synergy between many stakeholders. However, the sheer scale can lead to clutter. GCs often must verify whether a sub’s details are still current—some subs remain in the system after completing a job, even if they’ve moved on. For many, it’s still worth it: big GCs appreciate how BuildingConnected can get an entire office on the same page to collaborate on every job. Downtobid Key Features Here's the different features Downtobid has to address poor response rates from subs. Targeted Invites & Sub Engagement Downtobid helps GCs identify the correct subcontractors for each scope, boosting the chance they’ll see the invite and respond quickly. Personalized email templates display relevant details, so no one wastes time. Most ITB tools blast generic bid invite templates to as many contractors as possible, regardless of whether they’re the right fit. This "spray and pray" approach wastes everyone’s time. Contractors end up ignoring invites that don’t match their trade or location, and GCs are left scrambling to find qualified responses. Downtobid changes this with personalized bid invite templates. Using AI, Downtobid matches each project to the most relevant contractors, tailoring every invite to their expertise, region, and history. In fact, general contractors have reported a 30% increase in response rates from the right subcontractors after using these personalized bid invitation templates. National, Verified Subcontractor Database A huge subcontractor network is only useful if the information is accurate. Many platforms, including BuildingConnected, allow anyone to create an account, which leads to duplicate contacts, outdated entries, and contractors who are no longer active. GCs often waste hours reaching out to contacts who’ve moved companies or left the industry altogether. Downtobid solves this with a self-cleaning AI-powered subcontractor database . Rather than letting every user self-manage, Downtobid regularly checks and updates its data, reducing “verification successful waiting” problems. GCs don’t have to proceed blindly; they know each sub listing is relatively fresh, lowering risk. Simplified Planroom with AI-Sheeted Scopes One of the biggest frustrations for trade contractors is navigating cluttered planrooms. Contractors often receive ITBs with dozens of disorganized files, forcing them to flip through every sheet just to find what applies to them. This overwhelming process leads many to simply ignore invites altogether. Downtobid’s planroom eliminates this problem by AI-sheeting scopes. Documents are categorized and labeled so contractors can instantly find what they need without digging through irrelevant information. This comprehensive scope coverage helps trade contractors respond more confidently while ensuring GCs get bids that are accurate and timely. The planroom consists of four different folders: Plans Specs Photos Misc The simplified approach ensures the subs can access, review, and share construction documents quickly. Doing so helps the team keep up with the construction schedule and beat the due dates. This planroom also helps subs identify plans that are relevant to their trade reviewing hundreds of pages and can access it without creating an account. Automated Follow-ups & Tracking Instead of chasing replies, GCs rely on built-in triggers that remind subs about due dates. If a sub doesn’t open or respond by a certain time, Downtobid sends a polite nudge, giving GCs real-time updates on coverage without extra effort. No-Login Access & Simple Plan Sharing Subcontractors receive direct links—no complicated logins. That convenience fosters a connection built on trust, keeping the bidding process more human and less friction-filled. Straightforward Subcontractor Selection The success of a construction project relies heavily on the experienced team working together. The platform helps contractors connect with suitable and experienced subs. Downtobid does this by matching qualified subs to the specs. The tool leverages a multi-verification system to find subcontractors for its database so the contacts are all updated. The targeted subcontractor approach eliminates the need for mass mailing prospects hoping to land a subcontractor. It saves you the time of reviewing each subcontractor to find the right fit. You can also onboard your list of preferred subs or use Downtobid's list of pre-vetted commercial subcontractors . Pricing Plans Downtobid has two plans – free and paid membership plans. The free plan is suitable for smaller and simpler projects. The paid plans are of two categories. The first paid option costs $150 per user and has a bid coordinator. It’s suitable for medium projects. However, if you have a huge construction team and need 10 users, you can opt for our annual paid plan, priced at $300/m for a year. Simplify Bidding With AI If you’re tired of chasing bids and manual admin work, our AI analyzes your plans, creates personalized invites, and connects you with 57,000+ verified contractors within minutes. Building Connected Key Features Here are a few features that make Building Connected one of the best. Massive Subcontractor Network BuildingConnected boasts over 1 million trade contractors in its network, making it one of the largest platforms in the industry. For GCs managing complex, large-scale projects, this scale can be a huge advantage, providing access to niche trades and specialties. With a sprawling user base across multiple locations, BuildingConnected can support big GCs who need broad coverage. If you have labor needs in remote regions or specialized trades, it’s often a quick solution. However, because the network is open to anyone, it’s common to encounter outdated contacts, duplicate entries, or contractors who are out of business. GCs have also reported receiving bids from the wrong trades due to misclassification, which can derail the bidding process. Integrations & Collaboration Tools BuildingConnected connects seamlessly with Auto Desk and Procore, making it a central hub for builders who want cost analysis, scheduling, and plan updates integrated into a single calendar or dashboard. This feature is perfect for those who prefer saving their project documents and data on Auto Desk. It also serves as a backup in case you lose your construction data on Building Connected. You can read our full Building Connected reviews here. Prequal & Risk Management GCs can gather financials, safety stats, or references in one place, which helps mitigate risk before awarding. This is valuable for large or complex projects that demand thorough vetting. Enterprise-Level Ecosystem For GCs with an entire office of different departments, BuildingConnected’s broad suite of modules lets multiple teams stay on the same page—from design stakeholders to field coordinators—though some might find the system heavy if they only need basic coverage tracking. Pros ProCore integration Unlimited Users and file sharing Unlimited project bid packages Smart search Cons Outdated subs contact details No mobile app Messy planroom Generic bid packages These cons may make BuildingConnected not worth it . Pricing Plans Building Connected offers free and paid plans. The free plans have limited features, like limited bid management. The paid plan is priced per user and has many capabilities, like sending multiple bids. The cost of Building Connected varies. Unfortunately, Building Connected does not offer information about the pricing plan, and you must contact them to get this information. BuildingConnected vs. Downtobid: Features Compared Both BuildingConnected and Downtobid help GCs manage bid solicitation, but their approach to subcontractor coverage, bid engagement, and follow-ups makes them suited for different needs. Let’s break down how they compare: 1. Subcontractor Network & Coverage BuildingConnected: Huge network, great if you need to cast a wide net. But GCs must often verify who’s active or not, especially if user-generated profiles are outdated. Downtobid: Maintains a smaller yet more vetted subcontractor network, so GCs rarely waste time chasing defunct contacts. Winner: Tie—BuildingConnected for maximum scale, Downtobid for minimal “verification successful waiting.” 2. Bid Invite Engagement & Response Rates BuildingConnected: Mass invites can lead to many “maybes” or no-shows, requiring GCs to do more follow-up. Downtobid: Personalized invites, auto reminders, and simple plan links encourage subs to respond promptly. Winner: Downtobid, for a more direct connection that fosters actual engagement and fewer lost bids. 3. Risk Management & Data Oversight BuildingConnected: Offers prequal tools and optional takeoffs, beneficial for large coverage or formal awarding. Downtobid: Focuses on everyday coverage; GCs can still screen contractors, but it’s less about heavy compliance and more about building reliable partners. Winner: BuildingConnected, if you prioritize advanced risk checks and integrated cost analysis in one ecosystem. 4. Planroom Navigation & Subcontractor Experience Winner: Downtobid BuildingConnected’s planroom allows GCs to upload and share project files, but many subcontractors complain that the file organization is inconsistent. Without standardized structuring, subs often have to download entire plan sets just to locate the documents relevant to their trade, which slows down their response time. Downtobid solves this with AI-sheeted scopes, which automatically categorize and index project documents so subcontractors can quickly find what they need. By eliminating unnecessary downloads and confusion, subs can review projects faster, leading to higher bid participation. 5. Overall Bid Coverage & Workflow Efficiency Winner: Downtobid BuildingConnected’s high-volume approach means GCs can reach a lot of subcontractors, but bid coverage is inconsistent due to outdated contacts, mass invites, and a lack of follow-ups. This often leads to situations where GCs think they have enough coverage, only to find that many subs drop out or don’t respond at all. Downtobid prioritizes better bid coverage by ensuring that every ITB is relevant, responses are tracked, and follow-ups happen automatically. By the time bids are due, GCs have a clear, accurate view of who’s bidding and where coverage gaps exist, reducing last-minute stress. 6. User Experience & Human Touch BuildingConnected: Enterprise design; robust but can feel impersonal, especially for smaller GCs or single-trade invites. Downtobid: Maintains a simpler workflow, championing the human element. GCs see who’s reading the invite and get notifications if a sub doesn’t follow up, removing guesswork. Winner: Downtobid, especially for GCs who want a frictionless approach that respects each sub’s time. 7. Pricing & Overall Value BuildingConnected: Often described as higher cost for smaller teams. Larger builders might find its range of features worth it. Downtobid: Straightforward monthly plans that scale, good for GCs who want essential coverage tools without paying for big integrations. Winner: Downtobid, for straightforward affordability. BuildingConnected is strong if you justify the cost with advanced modules and enterprise usage. BuildingConnected vs. Downtobid: What Reddit Users Are Saying To understand how BuildingConnected and Downtobid stack up in real-world use, we explored this Reddit thread , where GCs, subcontractors, and estimators shared their honest experiences. Here’s what users had to say: BuildingConnected: Strengths and Weaknesses Many Redditors noted that BuildingConnected’s large network makes it a popular option, particularly for GCs handling out-of-state or large-scale projects. However, users often raised concerns about outdated data and issues with how subcontractors manage their own profiles. "The main issue with BuildingConnected is that they sold to Autodesk sometime a few years ago. It’s good if your subs are on it and used to it, but the biggest draw (network) is also their biggest weakness. They rely on subcontractors to manage their own data. If someone’s contact is out of date, I can’t change it. I can’t tell you how many times I have to follow up and call to see if these guys are bidding, only to find out that they’re either literally DEAD. The company doesn’t exist anymore.” Another user added: “BuildingConnected is better/more suited for GCs that do out-of-state work in my opinion.” Pricing was also brought up as a common concern: “They said that they had a great sub database. When we tried it out on a new project in Lexington, I got 3 bids. Half the contacts in there were expired and some of the trades are completely wrong (flooring guys listed as plumbers??).” Some users expressed frustration with Autodesk’s management of the platform: “Autodesk took it over, jacked up the price, and isn’t updating it. It’s still useful, but it feels like they’re more focused on monetizing than improving.” Downtobid: A New Alternative Though newer to the market, Downtobid has received positive feedback from Reddit users for its AI-powered features and focus on reliability. Users appreciated its ability to simplify workflows and improve the quality of connections with subcontractors. Downtobid's users highlighted the platform’s focus on reliable invites and automation. A GC shared, “We’ve seen a huge improvement in response rates since switching to Downtobid. The AI-driven process feels like a breath of fresh air.” A beta user shared: “I found a post here a few months ago. They were using AI to write ‘bid packages,’ and they sent personalized invites out. They’re called Downtobid, and I highly recommend their team—full disclosure, I am a beta tester right now, they are a new company but seem like they actually care.” Another user added: “Loving Downtobid so far!” While Downtobid doesn’t yet have the same scale as BuildingConnected, some users appreciated its emphasis on streamlined processes and targeted outreach: “Downtobid feels like it’s trying to solve the inefficiencies that come with larger platforms like BuildingConnected. The invites are more personalized, and it seems like they’re actually focusing on improving the user experience.” Takeaways From Reddit BuildingConnected: Some praise the vast network for big expansions, while others note the overhead of verifying out-of-date sub info. Large GCs appreciate the synergy with Autodesk but say it can feel bloated for smaller jobs. Downtobid: Users highlight how subcontractors respond more reliably due to simpler invites—“No login needed, real coverage.” They also like having fewer random invites “lost in the ether,” resulting in better final bids. Choosing the Right Platform Choose Downtobid if you value a human approach to coverage, prefer curated sub data, and want to reduce the complexity of chasing replies. It’s best for GCs who want to seamlessly share project details, confirm availability, and finalize bids without wrestling with massive extra modules. Choose BuildingConnected if your firm spans multiple locations, needs advanced synergy with Autodesk or Procore, or if you benefit from an all-in-one environment for cost analysis, prequalification, and big coverage blasts. It can unify your business across multiple departments so everyone stays on the same page, though you may need extra time to verify sub details. In short, if your projects demand enterprise-level collaboration tools and you have the cost tolerance, BuildingConnected can be a powerful system. But if you’re seeking a more nimble approach—where contractors quickly respond to relevant invites, coverage is easy to track, and you keep the bidding process personal—Downtobid might be your reliable partners solution. Final Thoughts Whether you’re using BuildingConnected or Downtobid, adopting digital bid management means fewer frantic phone calls, better doc-sharing, and a more efficient path to awarding. Both platforms help you gather bids from subcontractors, but they differ in how they handle risk, coverage, and data oversight. Evaluate your project scale, how many bids you typically run, and whether you need immediate synergy across your entire office. If so, BuildingConnected’s integrated environment may be beneficial. If you’d rather keep the process simpler—prioritizing human relationships, direct coverage, and minimal overhead—Downtobid delivers. Whichever tool you choose, the goal is to keep all stakeholders aligned on due dates and requirements, verifying that each sub is legitimate and ready to proceed. That’s how you ensure final success in this ever-evolving world of building and collaboration. BC Written by Bridget Cooper Published: Apr 9, 2024 Last updated: Aug 14, 2025 Have a Project? title: Preparing for October - GP Contract Changes
summary: Anima is built by doctors to be the fastest, safest way to manage patient requests. Combining online consultation with productivity tools, Anima brings everything a care team needs into a single platform.
body_text: The October 2025 deadline for the new GP contract mandate is fast approaching, and for many practices, it brings a sense of apprehension. The requirement to provide all-day online access can feel like opening the floodgates to unmanageable demand. A recent poll conducted during our webinar on this topic revealed that 76% of practices are not currently open all day and do not feel prepared for this change. But what if you could not only meet the mandate but also use it as an opportunity to enhance efficiency, take back control of your day, and improve patient care? Here’s how the Anima platform can help you turn this challenge into a sustainable operational model. 1. What is the GP Contract Mandate Asking of Medical Teams? From October, all GP practices in the UK will be required to offer patients online access for non-urgent appointments, medication queries, and administrative tasks during core hours (8:00 am to 6:30 pm). The goal is to improve patient access, providing a digital route for those who can use it, thereby freeing up phone lines for those who need them most. While the intention is positive, the practical reality raises concerns about managing a continuous flow of requests and preventing staff burnout to meet demands. 2. How Anima Supports All-Day Access Today Anima is a next-generation care enablement platform designed to manage patient demand efficiently through a single, integrated system. It replaces the traditional "8 am rush" with a structured, controlled, and all-day total triage system. The current data from our customers show that 92% of requests are resolved on the same day. When you compare that to the national average of 44.2%, that is a 2.1 times increase in capacity. The data also tells us that these requests are resolved from submission to completion within 57 minutes. Ultimately, supporting our practice teams to free up capacity, take back control of demands and save time. Here’s how Anima provides the framework to meet the mandate's requirements: Total triage in a single inbox: Anima handles all inbound patient requests, whether they are submitted online by the patient or taken over the phone by reception staff. Every request lands in one unified dashboard, creating a single, clear workflow for the entire team. Complete control over your hours: Your practice can set its operating hours to the mandated 8:00 am to 6:30 pm, or even extend them for specific request types, such as allowing administrative requests 24/7. You can even start accepting requests before 8:00 am so they are ready for your team when they arrive. EHR integration saves time: Anima integrates seamlessly with EMIS and SystmOne. This allows your team to view patient context, send messages, and book appointments directly into your live rota from a single screen, eliminating friction and the need to switch between different systems. 3. Leveraging Routine Requests to Control Demand The key to managing all-day access is not just being open, but controlling the flow of demand. Anima’s most powerful features are designed to help you do exactly that. Step 1: Set safe daily limits Within Anima, you can set daily limits for the number of medical and administrative requests your practice can safely handle based on your staffing levels for that day. For example, if you can handle 50 medical requests, the system will cap them once that number is reached. Step 2: Switch to 'Routine Only' mode with a safety net Once your daily limit for medical requests is met, Anima doesn't just shut off. Instead, it can be configured to only accept explicitly routine requests . This is the crucial safety net that allows you to remain compliant and accessible without being overwhelmed. To ensure patient safety, anyone submitting a routine request must first answer two mandatory screening questions: Is this an ongoing problem you've previously discussed with the practice? If they answer no, they are signposted to 111 or A&E. Acknowledgement of a non-urgent response time. The patient must acknowledge they can wait for a reply. Your practice can customize this expected response time (e.g., 24 or 48 hours), setting clear expectations from the start. These routine requests are clearly marked in the dashboard, and you can even filter them to appear last, allowing your team to prioritise urgent tasks first. Step 3: Close requests with unprecedented efficiency With Anima, practices resolve 92% of requests on the same day, with an average resolution time of just 57 minutes from submission. This is possible because: Better information upfront: The platform's structured questionnaires gather comprehensive information, and our AI assistant, Annie, provides a clear, easy-to-read summary for every case. All-in-one workflow: You can message the patient, assign the request to a colleague, refer to Pharmacy First, send patient education materials, and book an appointment without ever leaving the request screen. Smarter dispositions: Rich clinical data often shows that a request marked with red flags doesn't necessarily need a same-day appointment. This allows your team to allocate appointments more appropriately and protect valuable clinician time. This efficiency translates into achieving an inbox-zero by lunchtime and freeing up capacity equivalent to a 2.1x increase compared to the national average. You can also visit our recorded webinar for a full video walk-through of the above features. 👉 Webinar: Preparing for October - Are you ready for all day access? 4. Your Key Takeaways for October The upcoming mandate doesn't have to be a source of stress. With the right tools, your practice can meet the new requirements while creating a more controlled and efficient environment. Control is paramount: You can stay open all day by using daily limits and a safety-netted 'routine only' mode to protect your team. Routine & Acute requests funnel in differently, letting you prioritise care without being overwhelmed. Efficiency is built-In: A total triage system, deep EHR integration, and AI-powered summaries drastically reduce administrative burden and speed up request resolution. Now is the time to prepare: Start implementing the changes now so you can ensure your team is confident and fully prepared long before the October deadline. New to Anima? Book a free consultation below and we’d be happy to explore your practice’s specific needs.

body_text: EVI Industries Announces Participation at Jefferies Industrials Conference August 26, 2025 12:47 pm EDT Download as PDF MIAMI--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- EVI Industries, Inc. (NYSE American: EVI) announced today that Chairman and CEO, Henry M. Nahmad will present on behalf of the Company as well as host one-on-one meetings at the Jefferies Industrials Conference on Wednesday, September 3, 2025. For more information on the conference, or to schedule a one-on-one meeting, please contact your Jefferies sales representative. EVI is the largest value-added distributor of commercial laundry products and provider of related technical installation and maintenance services in North America. Since 2016, EVI has, among other things, completed thirty-one acquisitions, expanded into new geographies, retained and invested in additional sales and service personnel, broadened its OEM representations, and implemented advanced operating technologies. EVI maintains a founder-led management team with CEO, Henry M. Nahmad, and other executives and regional leaders that principally include founders of its acquired businesses, who collectively own more than 60% of the Company. EVI believes that its ownership and leadership structure allow management to operate with the necessary autonomy to maintain its focus on long-term value creation, including through industry consolidation, organic growth, and technological modernization. Since 2016, EVI has delivered a compounded annual growth rate in revenue, net income, and adjusted EBITDA of 31%, 18%, and 28%, respectively, while maintaining a low-leverage balance sheet that has positioned the Company to execute on strategic transactions. About EVI Industries EVI Industries, Inc., through its wholly owned subsidiaries, is a value-added distributor and a provider of advisory and technical services. Through its vast sales organization, the Company provides its customers with planning, designing, and consulting services related to their commercial laundry operations. The Company sells and/or leases its customers commercial laundry equipment, specializing in washing, drying, finishing, material handling, water heating, power generation, and water reuse applications. In support of the suite of products it offers, the Company sells related parts and accessories. Additionally, through the Company’s robust network of commercial laundry technicians, the Company provides its customers with installation, maintenance, and repair services. The Company’s customers include retail, commercial, industrial, institutional, and government customers. Purchases made by customers range from parts and accessories to single or multiple units of equipment, to large complex systems as well as the purchase of the Company’s installation, maintenance, and repair services. title: Proud to Be A Preferred Vendor for Visiting Angels
summary: Vitable continues as a 2025 preferred partner of Visiting Angels, providing caregivers with affordable, accessible health benefits and more.
body_text: At Vitable Health, we believe that better healthcare starts with everyday access, not red tape. That’s why we are proud to continue our role as a preferred partner of Visiting Angels Living Assistance Services , building on a consistent and trusted relationship with their franchise network over the years. For more than 25 years, Visiting Angels has been known as America’s Choice in Senior Home Care® . With more than 600 independently owned and operated franchise locations across the U.S. and internationally, the organization helps tens of thousands of families each year by providing compassionate, non-medical home care services. Their caregivers support seniors with everyday needs such as bathing, meal preparation, light housekeeping, and transportation, as well as specialized services like dementia care and respite care for family caregivers. Behind this vital care is a dedicated workforce of caregivers, individuals who give their time, energy, and compassion to make aging at home possible. But historically, too many caregivers have lacked access to affordable, meaningful health benefits. That’s where Vitable Health comes in. Supporting Caregivers with Better Health Benefits Through our partnership with Visiting Angels, Vitable Health offers an ACA-compliant, primary-care-first health benefits platform designed for today’s caregivers. Visiting Angels franchisees can offer their staff benefits that are: Affordable , with no co-pays, no deductibles, and no hidden fees. Accessible , with virtual primary care visits, mental health coaching, included prescriptions, and lab testing. Family-friendly , with dependent coverage available at no extra cost. These benefits are designed to be actually used, not avoided. For caregivers, this means having peace of mind and easy access to real care. For franchise owners, it means higher caregiver satisfaction, improved retention, and a stronger ability to recruit talent in a competitive industry. A Growing Partnership Across the Country To date, Vitable has partnered with dozens of Visiting Angels franchise organizations nationwide, offering a comprehensive suite of benefits designed to support caregivers and keep businesses compliant. These include: Individual Coverage Health Reimbursement Arrangement (ICHRA) : A flexible, tax-advantaged solution that allows employers to reimburse employees for individual health insurance plans, giving caregivers more choice in coverage. Minimum Essential Coverage (MEC) and Minimum Value Plan (MVP): Affordable plans that help franchises stay compliant with the Affordable Care Act while providing caregivers with access to essential health services. Vitable Primary Care (VPC) : Our core offering that ensures every member has built-in access to virtual primary care without co-pays or deductibles. Dental and Vision Coverage: Easy-to-use options that give caregivers access to preventive and restorative care for oral and eye health. Occupational Health : Convenient, compliance-focused services—including tuberculosis (TB) testing, screenings, and physicals—that help caregivers stay healthy, meet regulatory requirements, and continue delivering safe, reliable care. Together, these options make it easy for organizations of all sizes to find a plan that fits their budget while meeting the unique needs of their workforce. As an ongoing preferred partner in 2025, we are excited to deepen this relationship and continue supporting Visiting Angels’ caregiver-first mission, ensuring the workforce that delivers hope at home also receives the care and support they deserve. Building a Better Standard of Care At its heart, this partnership represents an alignment of values. Visiting Angels exists to provide compassionate, person-centered care for seniors. Vitable Health exists to provide simple, affordable healthcare for the everyday workers who make that care possible. Together, we are setting a new standard for what it means to support caregivers, because when caregivers are healthier and happier, the people they serve benefit too. Better care for caregivers. Better care for seniors. That’s the promise of our partnership.

title: Back-to-School, Back to Clean: Reset Your Routine with a Car Wash
summary: Start the school year fresh with a clean car. Discover car care tips, convenient washes, and ways to stay organized on the go.
body_text: As the back-to-school season approaches, life tends to pick up speed. Mornings become earlier, evenings fill with activities, and your car becomes your second home. Whether you’re managing school drop-offs, getting ready for the next semester or simply getting back into the rhythm of a daily commute, there’s no better time to refresh your space—and your mind—with a clean car. At Mister Car Wash, we know that cleaning goes beyond appearances. A freshly washed car helps set the tone for a fresh start. It’s about instilling feelings of confidence, calm, and readiness as you take on new challenges in a refreshing atmosphere. This enables you to focus, feel good, and move forward—no matter what the day brings. A Clean Car for Every Driver Back-to-school season isn’t just for students. It’s for parents juggling carpools, teens navigating their first solo drives, and college students packing up and heading off to campus. For every driver in the family, a clean car is a practical yet straightforward step that makes a noticeable difference in feeling and attitude. Think of it this way: Much like organizing school supplies or updating your calendar brings a sense of structure, getting your car cleaned signals a similar return to organization. It helps you feel in control. A cluttered car can add stress to an already busy day. A clean one gives you a sense of calm, and even a little pride as you pull into the school parking lot, the office, or make a quick grocery stop. Reset Your Car, Reset Your Mind Your car is your private retreat from the chaos of daily life. It’s where you plan the day, unwind between errands, and connect with your kids during after-school recaps. Taking time to reset that space—vacuuming the crumbs, wiping away the sunscreen smudges, and giving it a shine—can be rejuvenating. At Mister, we make it easy. Our Titanium Wash delivers a deep clean that protects your car’s finish and repels dirt and grime. It’s our most advanced wash yet—perfect for this season of fresh starts. Pair that with free vacuums , and you’ve got everything you need to feel refreshed inside and out. Car Care Tips for the School Year Looking to keep your car shining year long? Here are a few back-to-school car care tips from the Mister team: Vacuum regularly : With school lunches, sports gear, and food runs back in the mix, dirt and crumbs can pile up fast. Most Mister locations have free vacuums available to help you stay ahead of the mess. Keep cleaning wipes handy : Quick wipe-downs of dashboards, doors, and cup holders make a big difference in maintaining that clean feeling. Stay consistent with washes : As the seasons change, leaves, dust, and rain start to affect your exterior, keeping a regular wash schedule helps protect your vehicle’s finish. Maintain your shine: Our Titanium Wash adds bumper to bumper protection from the elements, and a mirror-like finish that keeps your car looking sharp, even during busy weeks. Convenience That Fits Your Routine We know time is tight during the school year. That’s why Mister Car Wash is designed for speed, quality, and convenience.
